title: Writing Your First Test
description: Create a simple test case, run tests, and interpret results.

slides.title: Where Tests Live 📁
slides.content:
Tests are typically placed in a `tests.py` file inside each app. Django’s `startapp` creates this file automatically. You can also organize tests into a `tests/` package with multiple modules.

A basic test looks like:

```python
from django.test import TestCase

class MyTest(TestCase):
    def test_something(self):
        self.assertEqual(1 + 1, 2)
```

Each method starting with `test_` is a test case.

slides.title: Running Tests
slides.content:
Run all tests in your project:
```bash
python manage.py test
```

Run tests for a specific app:
```bash
python manage.py test blog
```

Run a specific test class or method:
```bash
python manage.py test blog.tests.PostModelTest
python manage.py test blog.tests.PostModelTest.test_str_representation
```

Output shows dots for passing tests, `E` for errors, `F` for failures.

quizData.question: Which command runs all tests in the project?
quizData.explanation: `python manage.py test` is the command to run tests.

slides.title: A Simple Model Test
slides.content:
Assume you have a `Post` model with a `title` field. You can test that creating a post works:

```python
from django.test import TestCase
from .models import Post

class PostModelTest(TestCase):
    def test_create_post(self):
        post = Post.objects.create(title="Test")
        self.assertEqual(post.title, "Test")
        self.assertIsNotNone(post.id)
```

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use `setUp()` to avoid repetition

If many tests need the same data, define a `setUp()` method that creates test data. It runs before each test method.
